BombVault can now back up a server it does not run on. Add a VPS or any other Docker host as a node: it runs BombVault in a headless mode, needs no open port, and takes every order from this instance.

## ✨ Added

- **Nodes.** Under **Instances**, **Add node** names the server, picks where its backups go and hands you a compose file with its key filled in. The node talks to home over the relay through a private link of its own, and its backups never cross the relay.
- **Three places for a node's backups.** This instance's receiving server in append-only mode, so the node can add backups but never delete them. One of home's storage locations, with a sign-in made for the node. Or the node itself, behind a rest-server of its own, with home fetching a copy after each round. A small moving picture on each choice shows which way the backups travel.
- **Home runs the node.** Each node has a plan per section on its card, catches up on backups it missed while it was away, and raises one alert per failed run or time out of reach. The overview has a **Nodes** card, and **Backups** lists each node's containers and folder sets in a section of their own, where you add, edit, back up and restore them through home.
- **A rebuilt node comes back whole.** Start the same compose file on a new server and home takes the node on again, sends its placement and gives back its folder sets, container definitions and recent runs, so a missing container can be recreated from its backup.

## 🎨 Design

- **Follows GlimStone 4.8.2.** **Info** has four cards: Version, Components, Help and About. The Version card shows BombVault with its number and where updates stand, with **What's new** and **Check for updates** in one row, and Components lists rclone, restic and GlimStone, each number opening that project's newest release.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Fresh building blocks.** restic 0.20.0. When a restore sets owners by name and a user or group name cannot be resolved, restic falls back to the numeric owner from the snapshot instead of handing the file to root. A restore also refuses snapshots with duplicate or out-of-order names, and the index needs less memory. The image also picks up the security updates Debian has already published, among them glibc and zlib.
- **Every instance card says what it is.** A small caption under the name reads This instance, Member, ZFS server, Android app or Node, in the same style on every card.
- **A picked option looks the same everywhere.** It fills with the accent colour, and the frame and the round dot beside it are gone. That covers the node's backup place, Storage, and the windows for restoring, removing and moving.
- **The folder picker on phones.** Its buttons stay clear of a window's Cancel and Save, and the list keeps its height while a folder loads.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Snapshot holds are counted safely.** BombVault reads the number of holds ZFS reports on a snapshot at its full 64-bit size and no longer narrows it to a smaller integer.

## 🌐 Translations

- **Nodes in every language.** The new pages are translated into all 42 languages and the docs into all 26, and "instance", "relay" and "storage location" follow the glossary everywhere.
